prose: A long essay argues that the claim AI is inevitable is a thought-terminating cliche worth dismantling rather than accepting. Nobody knows ahead of time which technologies a society will develop or adopt, so calling any specific future inevitable is unfalsifiable prophecy, not analysis.

In hindsight every successful technology looks inevitable, the piece notes, but that says nothing: the iPhone's exact shape was not preordained, and at most something with a vague family resemblance might have arrived in any number of forms. Treating inevitability as an argument, the author contends, is a way of telling people to stop thinking and get with the program.
highlights: 'AI is inevitable' called a thought-terminating cliche
No one can know which technologies will be adopted
Hindsight makes every winner look preordained
The iPhone could have taken many forms
Inevitability talk functions as a demand to comply
